extracted.intended_audience: prospective improv students (Los Angeles) — beginners through advanced improvisers looking for classes or drop-ins
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for choosing and enrolling in improv classes at a Los Angeles improv school, including placement advice, prerequisites for different class tiers (intro/bitness/advanced), drop-in rules, intensives application, and discount policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advanced Courses — eligibility (4+ classes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Classes for advanced improvisers (4+ classes done at any long-form improv theater).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Described as 'Our improv grad school.' Advanced courses include specialized offerings (e.g., Finding Your Comedic Voice, Musical Improv for Advanced Improvisers, Advanced Flow) with multi-week formats and prices listed. Several advanced classes are listed as 'sold out' with 'join wait list' options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intensives — must apply; advanced students
rubrics_metrics.description: A week long WGIS sampler for advanced students. Must apply: https://forms.gle/naSwnbyEdaW5XtP36.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intensives are multi-day (listed as 4 classes, 1 show), priced (e.g., $375 USD), and targeted at advanced students; specific sessions (July, August) are shown as sold out/waitlist. Application is required to attend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intro Levels — placement guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Our core classes. If you have experience at any long-form improv theater, skip level 1. If you have never studied game, start at level 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core levels are named/defined (Level 1: Intro To Improv; Level 2: Game of the Scene; Level 3: Harold Structure). Each level lists session count and often includes a culminating show (e.g., '6 classes, 1 show' or '8 classes, 1 show').

rubrics_metrics.name: Level 1/2/3 — course focuses
rubrics_metrics.description: Level 1: Intro To Improv; Level 2: Game of the Scene; Level 3: Harold Structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Level-specific instructors, dates, prices, and session lengths are provided. Placement advice (see Intro Levels) determines which level a student should take; classes usually run multiple weeks and commonly include a final show.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bitness — focus on reps; intermediate eligibility (3+ classes)
rubrics_metrics.description: These classes focus on reps over notes. 'Bitness' is a pun on fitness. For intermediate improvisers (3+ classes at any long-form theater).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bitness offerings include multiple time-slot variants (Noon, After-Noon, Night) with different class counts and prices (examples: 12 classes, 1 show; 9 classes, 1 show; 8 classes, 1 show). Emphasizes practice/repetition rather than lecture-style notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empathy classes — focus and classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Jim Woods special 'empathy' classes focus on authentic acting. 'Empathy' courses are now listed in the 'Advanced' section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empathy-driven improv is treated as an advanced specialty track (examples appear under 'Currently Running' and 'Advanced Refresher' listings). Expect acting-oriented exercises and multi-week formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drop-ins — prerequisite two levels
rubrics_metrics.description: Get a few reps. Must have two levels of improv classes from any school.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drop-ins are single-class opportunities (listed dates and instructors) with a consistent low fee (e.g., $16 USD). Intended for students who already have basic training (two levels) and want additional practice without committing to a full course.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-day workshops — expert one-and-done format
rubrics_metrics.description: Short on time? Try these expert one-and-done workshops.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One-day workshops are positioned as intensive single-day offerings for focused skill work. The listing currently shows 'No one-day workshops coming up.' When offered, these are taught by experts and are separate from multi-week courses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discount policy — last-minute financial-need spots
rubrics_metrics.description: We sometimes offer discounts on last-minute spots for those in financial need.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students in financial need may contact the school (classes@wgimprovschool.com) or check community/social pages for occasional last-minute discounts. This is situational and not a guaranteed standard discount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course structure — session counts and shows
rubrics_metrics.description: Most classes list a number of sessions and often include a show (e.g., '6 classes, 1 show', '8 classes, 1 show', '4 classes').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect multi-week courses to culminate in a performance opportunity; session counts and whether a show is included vary by course and level. Pricing is tied to session length (examples provided alongside each course).
